To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
L. pneumophia modulates the transcriptional response in hMDMs by down-regulating protein synthesis pathways, and by up-regulating inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and metabolic pathways.
L. pneumophlia infection of hMDMs results in a global transcriptional response that is primarily associated with immune response and metabolic and nutritional pathways.
the hMDM transcriptome of L. pneumophilia-infected cells is predominated by upregulation of inflammatory pathways, anti-apoptosis and downregulation of protein synthesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcriptional response to Legionella pneumophia infection in human monocyte-derived macrphages.
the transcriptional response in hMDMs to the ankB mutant and wild type L. pneumophia.
the identification of the host cell response to L. pneumoniae and its modulation by virulence determinants of L. pneumoniae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transcriptional response to infection by actively-replicating L. pneumophilia and the non-replicative mutant is similar and involves modulation of the host inflammatory response and metabolic pathways.
the L. pneumophia-induced hMDM transcription response is a complex and highly orchestrated event that involves a wide variety of metabolic pathways.
L. pneumophia modulates hMDM gene expression to promote its intracellular survival and proliferation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
L. pneumophia modulates the hMDM transcriptome to promote its own proliferation, but also to suppress the host immune response and metabolic pathways.

the hMDM transcriptome is primarily modulated by the host response to the infection and that the L. pneumophia Dot/Icm type-IV translocation system plays a minimal role in this transcriptional response.
AnkB is an essential effector for L. pneumophia replication within hMDMs, and AnkB is required for L. pneumophilia to modulate the hMDM transcriptome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
L. pneumophia is a master regulator of the host immune response, which is not dependent upon its ability to actively replicate within macrophages.
the transcriptional response is not dependent on bacterial replication.
